p66: Whenever something outlandish and Magecraft-related happened in Fuyuki, Kotomine would be one of the ones going out to hypnotize officials to report the events as a hallucination or mundane accident. But even if you convinced the public, there would always be one person who would be suspicious. But even if they had suspicions, without solid proof, it wouldn’t matter what they thought. And so the cycle had gone on. Things happen, Church and Association cover them up, and suspicious people would grumble.
p67: And then Sonic and Dr. Eggman happened.
p68: They were loud, in-your-face, and most of all, blatant. The only way to cover them up would be to cast a memory spell over the entire city, and no Mage alive today had that kind of power. And even if they did, the news feeds had already been posted online by dozens of eager nerds. Their very presence had viewers questioning everything they thought they knew about their world. Although no one really understood it yet, the veil of secrecy was gone. The old excuses were no longer holding water. The people wanted real answers.

p198: After being forcibly relocated into the warehouse, Rin had gone into what was known as The Funk. While intellectually, she knew that it was more pragmatic to avoid a direct confrontation and let everyone else handle the hard stuff. After all, the general tactic for Masters was to allow their Servants to take the lead in battles, supporting only from a distance. That was how her father fought in the Fourth War (she assumed).
p199: But huddling in some hidey-hole was not something she approved of. The fact that it was something Shinji would do only served to increase her irritation. And if there was one thing Tohsaka prided herself on, it was not being like Shinji. She had felt a presence leave the Boundary Field, which she assumed was the seaweed-headed twerp fleeing the battle like the coward he was. That alleviated her despondent attitude somewhat—while Shinji was busy bailing, Archer had forced Rin to go into hiding.
p200: However, the small guilt she felt, for being on the sidelines while her friends—allies, the mage within her whispered assertedly, they were only allies of convenience—fought with all of their might, did not diminish. Besides, it was a bit creepy listening to all of the explosions and not seeing what was causing them.
p201: Rin then realized that her fists weren’t shaking because of any guilt or anger. They were shaking because the floor was shaking!
p202: The ground erupted, and Rin just barely jumped back in time to avoid being hit by the pieces. What looked like a gigantic drill was poking out of the ground, and it rose, revealing that it was on top of some metal sphere with robotic legs, which clambered out of the hole like some sort of spider that evolved to mine instead of spin webs. The drill split apart, manipulated by smaller arms. They spun around the sphere, revealing that it was in fact a vehicle—driven by none other than Dr. Eggman!
d303: Eggman: Heh heh heh...According to my sensors, the source of the energy field is around here somewhere...
d303_note: Eggman muttered, typing away at his console.
p203: Eggman glanced up, and even from a distance Rin could see his eyes narrow underneath those glasses.
p204: Uh-oh. It didn’t take a genius to figure out where this was going. Rin’s first instinct was to call for Archer. But Archer was the only one protecting the harbor from the submarine’s missiles (Seriously, who put gun turrets and rocket launchers on a vehicle designed for underwater travel?!). If she called him in, however briefly, it may be too long before another salvo was unleashed.
p205: But more importantly…Rin wanted to face Eggman on her own. Her ancestors used to control the land that would become Fuyuki. The Heaven’s Feel was only allowed to take place because of their permission. And even after the city was built, it was still considered their territory, by the Mage’s Association, if not by Japan’s government. And as the last of the Tohsakas (Save one, whispered a dark spot in her mind), Rin felt it was her responsibility to deal with any intruders that threatened it. And if she didn’t do it herself…what kind of Mage would she be?
p206: The dark spot in Rin’s head raised its voice, pointing out that Eggman’s vehicle was probably loaded with a plethora of futuristic weapons. Rin’s pride as a mage, honed through years of training, countered with the rebuttal:
d305: Rin: So what? I’ve got Magecraft. Everyone knows Magecraft trumps all.
p207: What about the old reports of Mages being killed by mere guns—
d308: Rin: I’m about to be awesome!
p208: During this mental debate, Eggman had pointed dramatically at Rin.
d309: Eggman: Unless my scanners are glitching—unlikely, given that they were made by the smartest being in the universe, IE, me—all of this energy is coming from you!
d310: Eggman: You’ve got a Chaos Emerald, all right! Hand it over!
d311: Rin: And what if I refuse?
d311_note: Rin asked, reaching into her pouch.
p209: She fingered several gems, each loaded with a powerful spell. As far as she knew, mages weren’t very commonplace in Sonic’s world. It was possible that Eggman hadn’t met one, even with his fancy-schmancy ‘Magecraft radar’. If he believed that whatever was happening was due to the Emeralds, all the better.
d312: Eggman: Then I’ll just take you with me.
d313: Eggman: And the passenger seat has a very tight harness!
audio_title13: Fate/stay night [Réalta Nua] (PS Vita) OST - Burst Up (2012)
p210: With speed and aim that would make the best in the Wild West green with envy, Rin pointed her finger at Eggman and fired a jewel loaded with a spell far more potent than Gandr. It was one of her more recent breakthroughs—combining the energy of the Power Rings with her own jewel Magecraft. One could argue (like Archer had) that all Rin did was squeeze the gem into the Ring’s hole, but Rin knew that it took very precise calculations to make sure that the gem’s power would not cause the whole array to self-destruct from the contrast of abilities; decay and protection did not normally go hand in hand. But Rin had pulled it off—and now it was time to see how well it would work on the field.
p211: The explosion was pretty phenomenal, as far as Rin was concerned. There was no comparing a normal gem to one imbued with Power Ring energy. But when the smoke cleared, it was revealed that one of the drill pieces had shielded the madman! And worse, the blasted thing only looked badly burnt!
d314: Eggman: That was a pretty good trick, but not good enough.
d315: Eggman: Now it’s my turn. Get a load of this!
p212: The ‘Egg Cracker’ thundered forward, and under less dangerous circumstances would have looked comical. Its spider-legs stamping about reminded Rin of footage she had seen about the probe the Americans had sent to Mars. But she also saw that if she didn’t move, she would be trampled underneath.
p213: So she Reinforced her legs. With her Mage Circuits coursing with energy, Rin leapt high into the air, kicked off of the wall, and shot across the warehouse over Eggman. Once she landed, she fired a regular Gandr at Eggman’s head. While the drill shields weren’t fast enough to block the gem, the glass dome covering the doctor’s cockpit was protection enough. All her attack did was get Eggman’s attention.
d316_note: Eggman shouted, and redirected the Egg Cracker at her.
p214: But rather than just charging, a port opened up on its front. There was a sound like a cannon being fired, and out from the port a small ball rocketed out. A ball with spikes. Rin had to jump to the side to avoid being hit, and kept jumping as Eggman fired more and more spike balls at her. But as she darted, one of the metal arms lunged forward and struck her dead-on.
p215: Rings fell from Rin’s body as she was sent flying up into the air. Eggman’s horrible laughter was mixed in with the sound of Rin hitting the floor, and she slid against the wall.
p216: Grimacing, Rin struggled to get up. Though undamaged, she felt the metal hitting her side. And if her brief flight hadn’t broken a rib, she would be very surprised. She saw Eggman’s mech stomp over to her, the light shining creepily off of Eggman’s glasses.
d317: Eggman: Now, I’d like to keep having fun, but I’ve got a schedule to keep.
d318: Eggman: Either you give me the Chaos Emerald, or I start searching!
p217: To illustrate this threat, extra robot tentacles, with metal claws and clamps like the ones Arms had, but smaller, extended from the Egg Cracker.
p218: Rin gritted her teeth, and refused to be intimidated.
d319: Rin: I don’t have your stupid Emerald, you perverted old geezer!
d319_note: She shouted, and fired another Ring-Gem at Eggman.
p219: She missed his head, but managed to blast off one of the claws.
d320_note: Eggman yelled, ducking out of reflex. Poking his head up, he muttered.
d321: Eggman: Note to self, leave the auto-shield on…huh? Where’d she go?
p220: Spinning in the air with all the grace and skill of a kung fu master, she aimed a Reinforced leg to kick off Eggman’s bald head.
p222: A punching glove on a metal spring popped out and slammed into Rin’s stomach. Rin felt the wind leave her, and she fell once more.
d324: Eggman: Didn’t you watch all of those PSAs on the danger of pretending to be Sonic?
d325_note: Rin thought bitterly, punching the ground. She had never felt so humiliated before in her entire life.
p223: For the past ten years, she had trained herself rigorously. She honed her Magecraft to the finest imaginable, preparing and empowering the highest-grade gems. Practiced martial arts with techniques impossible to finish without Reinforcing her body. And while she knew that it would be impossible for a mortal being to combat a Servant, that was why she summoned Archer. However, for all other dangers, she had felt that her abilities could handle anything.
p224: But now, when she needed it the most, when it was time to solve the crumbling situation, her Magecraft failed her. Everything she had been taught to believe in…useless. She had been outdone, by cold machines…again.
p225: Bitterly, she looked down at the floor. Her eyes focused on the Command Seals on the back of her hand. Gritting her teeth, she began to focus. The marks started to glow.
d326_note: Eggman grunted, before a massive flash of light filled the room.
p226: When the shine faded, a tall, dark and handsome stranger stood between the evil scientist and the damsel in distress.
d327: Archer: Here I come, to save the day.
